_meta.status: TRIAL - NOT IN THE CHAIN. The sealed foundation-cohort anchors reproduce on iamatlas_celltype_markers_v0_2.json; adopting this file requires re-sealing them and re-measuring the per-entry healthy references.
_meta.criterion: at each address, the margin is the beta distance from this cell type to its NEAREST measured rival (not to the mean of the others). The old v0_2 criterion, |target - mean(other celltypes)|, scored a globally extreme address highly for every cell type in which it was extreme, which is why 33.8% of its markers served more than one panel.
_meta.rival_set: the cell types measured at that address. The atlas is sparse per address (median 25 of 115 cell types measured, range 6-84), so a margin is against the measured rivals and the count is recorded.
known_limits: Atlas coverage per cell type ranges from 252 addresses (megakaryocyte, eosinophil, monocyte, neutrophil, erythroblast, small_intestine and three others) to 482,421. A cell type with a 252-address pool cannot have an exclusive 300-marker panel; this is a property of the atlas, not of the criterion.
22 of 115 entries do not reach 20 markers at this margin and are marked individually_resolvable=false - their readings should be made at group level or withheld.

Per-entry healthy spread widens slightly against v0_2 (median 0.074 vs 0.066 across 40 healthy donors). Part of v0_2's apparent tightness came from entries sharing markers: correlated panels give correlated readings, which look tighter without being more about the cell.
